tasks.context: The MCP function (supabase/functions/mcp/index.ts) only exposes 3 read-only tools: list_groups, list_instructions, get_production_instruction. An agent connected via MCP cannot create or modify instructions — it can only read. This severely limits the product's value proposition of 'version-controlled instructions managed by agents'.

Add update_instruction tool — creates a new instruction_versions row (never mutates existing versions)
Add delete_instruction tool — soft delete (set archived=true), not a hard delete
All new tools require authentication (ctx.isAuthenticated())
All new tools use user-scoped Supabase client (not service role)
Add Zod input validation matching the DB schema
Update src/lib/mcp/index.ts (the source file — the function is auto-generated from it)

tasks.title: Add health check endpoint + Telegram webhook resilience
tasks.context: The Telegram webhook has no cheap health endpoint and firecrawlScrape() has no bounded retry/backoff: any non-2xx response or exception immediately drops URL ingestion. Keep health/readiness and transient Firecrawl retry behavior here; Telegram secret validation, update_id idempotency, and edited-message semantics are covered by IH-004.
acceptance_criteria: Expose a cheap authenticated/unauthenticated health check that reports dependency readiness without invoking Firecrawl or the LLM.
Add bounded retry/backoff for transient Firecrawl failures and return a stable response without duplicate inserts.
Add tests for timeout, non-2xx, and dependency-missing paths.
tasks.review_notes: 2026-08-12: verified in supabase/functions/telegram-webhook/index.ts; no agent implementation to review.
tasks.evidence: Source review 2026-08-13: telegram-webhook has no health route and Firecrawl is a single fetch with immediate null/failure handling; no bounded retry/backoff.

tasks.title: Verify deployed profiles RLS blocks cross-user reads and add regression coverage
tasks.context: Concrete audit finding: supabase/migrations/20260307174057_3fba95de-96c5-4591-92ff-a089d60ec7cd.sql creates the authenticated SELECT policy "Users can view all profiles" with USING (true). A later own-profile policy does not neutralize it because permissive policies are ORed. Profiles contain user_id and Telegram-link metadata, so another authenticated user may read other users' profile rows. Preserve service-role webhook lookups while restricting user-scoped access.
acceptance_criteria: Verify deployed policies, not only migration text.
Authenticated user A cannot SELECT user B profile rows or sensitive link fields.
Regression test fails if the permissive historical policy is reintroduced.
tasks.review_notes: 2026-08-12: migration history contains the restrictive own-profile policy, but deployed-policy verification and regression coverage remain unverified; no agent implementation to review.
tasks.description: Confirm the deployed policies do not retain any permissive profiles SELECT policy; add an authenticated cross-user read regression test and document the migration verification.
tasks.evidence: Source review 2026-08-13: migration 20260709190732 drops the historical profiles USING(true) policy and creates owner-only SELECT. No deployed-policy verification or cross-user regression test is present in the inspected tree.

tasks.title: Make Atlas Cloud asset transfers bounded and fail-fast
tasks.context: scripts/atlas_cloud.py uses curl for upload/download. download() uses -s --retry 3 without --fail, connect timeout, or max time; upload() similarly lacks bounded timeout/error handling. Non-empty HTTP error bodies can be accepted as downloaded assets, and stalled transfers can hang a job.
acceptance_criteria: Upload and download use explicit connect and overall timeouts plus HTTP fail-fast behavior.
Retries are bounded and do not retry non-transient 4xx responses.
Tests prove HTTP error bodies cannot be accepted as successful assets.

tasks.title: Make the court explorer use one live/curated source of truth
tasks.context: The explorer data layer correctly loads Supabase `courts_with_stats` with a bounded timeout and falls back to the curated launch catalog. However, app/courts/page.tsx always server-renders launchCourts with source="curated" and relies on a later client fetch of /api/courts. Separately, app/page.tsx embeds another hardcoded court array. This creates first-render/stale-catalog drift and duplicate court identity data.
acceptance_criteria: Server-render /courts from loadExplorerCourts() and pass the actual source, while retaining a bounded client refresh if needed.
Remove or centralize the root-page hardcoded court records so court names/IDs/counts cannot diverge from the canonical catalog.
Keep the curated fallback explicit in UI and preserve the honest zero-counter behavior.
Add tests covering Supabase success, timeout/error fallback, source labeling, and the root/explorer shared court identity.
Verify the public courts_with_stats contract exposes only intended aggregate/public fields and document the deployed RLS/view assumption.
tasks.description: Remove the live-vs-curated first-render mismatch and duplicate homepage catalog before adding more growth surfaces.
tasks.evidence: Source review 2026-08-14: courts/page.tsx passes launchCourts/source curated; client refreshes /api/courts; supabase-courts.ts loads courts_with_stats; root app/page.tsx contains a separate embedded Court[] array.

tasks.title: Replace broad public table reads with safe public projections
tasks.context: The reviewed migrations grant SELECT USING(true) on profiles, check_ins, plans, matches_1v1, and run_rsvps. src/lib/db.ts then calls profiles.getAll() and joins full profile rows into public activity. This exposes more than the product needs and makes privacy changes difficult.
acceptance_criteria: Create safe views or column-limited RPCs for public court presence, schedules, leaderboards, and match summaries.
Remove or narrow base-table SELECT policies for sensitive profile/activity columns while preserving intended public functionality.
Add authenticated regression tests proving a client cannot read private profile fields or unrelated user metadata.
Update src/lib/db.ts to consume the safe projection instead of profiles.getAll() joins.
tasks.description: Make public presence genuinely public-by-design, not full-row database access.
tasks.evidence: 2026-08-15 source review: profiles and activity tables have permissive SELECT USING(true); adapter fetches all profiles for public joins.

tasks.title: Make match submission and ELO application server-authoritative
tasks.context: matches_1v1 INSERT/UPDATE policies allow either participant to write, and 20260302043421 attaches rating-changing triggers to INSERT and UPDATE. The client adapter calls direct table inserts. This is vulnerable to forged scores, unauthorized state transitions, and repeated rating changes.
acceptance_criteria: Add a single validated RPC for submitting a match and a separate confirmation/dispute transition.
Ensure a match result can apply ELO at most once; score/winner fields become immutable after submission except through an explicit dispute flow.
Validate both participants, court scope, score bounds, and authenticated caller server-side.
Remove direct client writes that bypass the RPC and add regression tests for replay, forged participant IDs, and unauthorized updates.
tasks.description: Protect competitive integrity by making the write path and rating side effects authoritative and idempotent.
tasks.evidence: 2026-08-15 source review: either participant can INSERT/UPDATE matches_1v1; AFTER INSERT and AFTER UPDATE triggers mutate profile ratings; client writes directly.

tasks.title: Enforce active check-in lifecycle and court-scoped realtime
tasks.context: check_ins expire_at is only filtered in client queries; create() directly inserts and defaults courtId to court1. The realtime subscription listens to all check_ins changes with no court filter. This conflicts with the court-scoped architecture and can produce duplicate/stale presence.
acceptance_criteria: Make courtId required for all public adapter mutations and remove sentinel court1 defaults.
Add a database-enforced active check-in invariant and an atomic check-in/out or upsert path.
Add cleanup/archive behavior for expired rows and tests for duplicate active check-ins and expiry.
Scope realtime subscriptions to the selected court and avoid refreshing unrelated courts.
tasks.description: Make presence accurate and cheap at the database boundary, not just in client filters.
tasks.evidence: 2026-08-15 source review: expires_at is client-filtered; create() directly inserts; most adapter methods default to court1; onChanges subscribes table-wide.

tasks.title: Bound Telegram ingestion cost and payload abuse
tasks.context: supabase/functions/telegram-webhook/index.ts performs synchronous Firecrawl and LLM work from a public POST body, with no request-size cap, URL host/scheme policy, timeout budget, or per-chat rate limit. The handler writes with service role after resolving a linked chat. Add guardrails without duplicating IH-004 secret validation/update_id ownership.
acceptance_criteria: Reject oversized Telegram updates and bound extracted text before external calls.
Accept only http/https URLs and document any allowed host policy; do not fetch arbitrary local/file/data URLs.
Enforce bounded external-call timeouts and one bounded retry only for transient Firecrawl failures.
Add a durable per-chat rate-limit or quota check before Firecrawl/LLM work, with tests for rejection and allowed paths.
Do not bypass RLS or expose service-role credentials; preserve IH-004 secret and update_id requirements.
tasks.evidence: Source review 2026-08-16: handler accepts POST JSON after method check, extracts arbitrary https? URL, calls Firecrawl synchronously, and classifies up to 8,000 chars; no visible body cap, timeout, host policy, or rate limit.
